name: Hack the Planet
author: Multiverse Video editors
description: Understand systems well enough to defend, repair, and improve them.

items.note: A plain-language walkthrough of threat modeling: who might want your data, what they could do with it, and which protections are worth your effort.
A hackerspace workshop on hardware hacking for absolute beginners: how to open a device, find its debug ports, and learn what's inside.
A podcast episode with European Digital Rights on the trade-off between online safety laws and privacy, from the PublicSpaces coalition.
One short lesson from Techlore's free Go Incognito course: what actually protects your traffic on a network, and what doesn't.
Crowd Supply's Teardown Sessions talks with Michael Altfield, maker of BusKill, a laptop kill-cord, about practical OpSec and privacy hardware.
A NorthSec talk on fitting threat modeling into fast development cycles, so security questions get asked while the design can still change.
Five concrete email-security rules from a digital-security hotline expert, framed around the phishing campaigns that target journalists and activists.
Shows how the Wi-Fi network names your devices broadcast can be mapped back to a home address, then what you can do about it.
A talk from CIRCL's MISP training channel on putting the open-source MISP threat-intelligence platform to work inside an incident response plan.
A step-by-step solve of a crackmes.one reverse-engineering challenge, narrated so you can follow the reasoning, not just the answer.
